newsitem.title: THAILAND: Latest Thai finance merger heralds liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Latest Thai finance merger heralds liberalisation.

text.p: A decision by three Thai finance firms to merge and form a new bank was widely welcomed on Thursday as a sign the nation's financial liberalisation process is gathering momentum, analysts and executives said.

Major local broker Nava Finance and Securities Plc, CMIC Finance and Securities Plc and Thaimex Finance and Securities Plc will create a new 140 billion baht ($5.4 billion) entity, which will apply for a bank licence.
The marriage was the first to take place after the central bank offered new incentives to firms in the finance sector to consolidate and merge for better efficiency.
Thai authorities last month revamped the finance sector, which was hit by billions of dollars in sour loans lent to the liquidity-hit and depressed domestic property sector.
"I think the big picture story is that this is the beginning of a trend to fully liberalise," said Stephen Hill, head at WI Carr, Nava's foreign securities trading partner.
Under existing laws foreigners are limited to a maximum 25 percent stake in Thai finance firms or banks and a maximum 49 percent in securities companies.
Nava and Thaimex are subsidiaries of Thai Military Bank Plc, Thailand's sixth largest commercial bank in asset terms, while CMIC is controlled by Thai Farmers Bank Plc, the country's third largest.

Central bank rules forbid Thai commercial banks from holding more than a 10 percent stake in another bank and raise the possibility that foreign shareholders may come into the new merged bank, Hill said.

"This could open the door to the relaxation of foreign ownership laws in the Thai financial sector. I think we are now not far from total liberalisation whereby foreigners can buy potentially up to 100 percent of all these companies," he said.
Analysts expressed surprise that subsidiaries from two separate banks were set to join forces.

"I was a bit surprised to see CMIC joining this process. In my opinion that is an indication of CMIC's management independence from Thai Farmers Bank...and that the Bank of Thailand is serious about mergers," said Suraphol Thipvilai, assistant research manager at Vickers Ballas.

Thai Military Bank's unlisted subsidiaries, Thanapol Finance and Securities Plc, Thai Thanakorn Finance and Securities Co Ltd and Bangkok Asian Securities Co Ltd, were likely to join the group, analysts said.
Combined assets would then be around 180 billion baht, making the group the size of a lower-middle sized Thai bank and eligible to apply for a new licence.

Even so, unless other firms joined the group, the limited size of the likely group's asset base raised doubts about the entity's ability to compete in an increasingly combative Thai banking environment, analysts said.
Of concern is the future of foreign securities partners. To merge, firms must first split their finance and securities arms.
CMIC is tied to Merrill Lynch, Nava is linked with WI Carr and recently-acquired Standard Chartered Securities to form Nava SC Securities.
Hill said WI Carr's happy relationship with Nava would continue for the time being but the company was constantly looking to expand its business.
